old: *azt* *hiszem* (\"I think, I believe\") is built from *hisz* (\"to believe\") in its definite form *hiszem*, plus *azt*, the accusative of *az* (\"that\") pointing forward to the idea that follows. Unlike an English \"I believe that...\", no *hogy* is needed — the clause just follows directly after a comma. You've already heard *Károly* and others say it in earlier lessons; now you know exactly how it's built.
new: You know *azt* *hiszem* (\"I think, I believe\") from stating opinions in earlier lessons. It is built from *hisz* (\"to believe\") in its definite form *hiszem*, plus *azt*, the accusative of *az* (\"that\") pointing forward to the idea that follows. You already use it with *hogy* (*Azt hiszem, hogy ...*); in everyday speech *hogy* is often dropped and the clause simply follows after a comma.
why: screen presented azt hiszem as new and said no hogy is needed, contradicting a2-58 which taught azt hiszem, hogy

old: *azt* *hiszem* itself drops *hogy*, but a question built around it — *Azt* *hiszed*, *hogy*...? — can still use *hogy*, because now *hiszed* is the main verb of a real question, not just an opinion-opener sitting in front of a statement.
new: *Azt* *hiszem*, *hogy*... and *Azt* *hiszem*, ... mean the same: *hogy* is optional. In a question, *Azt* *hiszed*, *hogy*...? normally keeps it.
why: tip said azt hiszem "drops hogy"; make it consistent with a2-58 and the new text
